mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2% within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% within the last two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts related industries and increases economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% within the last month signals a weakening supply side, which may indicate a slowdown in economic activity and lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) by more than 0.5% per month for two consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which may lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% per month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) by more than 1% per quarter signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 jobs per month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) increase by more than 1% per quarter and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% within the last two months, it signals a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% per quarter and HOUST increases > 5% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 and HOUST increases on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
